translationRepairs: Chancellor Chen Jia and others submitted: 'Your Majesty perpetually reflects on the path of filial piety, establishing the Dance of Illustrious Virtue to illuminate Emperor Xiaowen's abundant virtue—all of this exceeds what we foolish ministers can fathom.

Chancellor Jia and others submitted: 'Your Majesty perpetually reflects on the path of filial piety, establishing the Dance of Illustrious Virtue to illuminate Emperor Xiaowen's abundant virtue—all of this exceeds what we foolish ministers can fathom.
Source names only 丞相臣嘉; Chen is not in the Chinese and invents a surname absent from this unit.

Chamberlain for Law Xin Jin and the chancellor proposed: "When officials or other ranked personnel receive food and drink from subordinates under their supervision, jurisdiction, administration, or command, and the amount merely repays expenses, no charge should be brought.

Chamberlain for Law Xin and the chancellor proposed: "When officials or other ranked personnel receive food and drink from subordinates under their supervision, jurisdiction, administration, or command, and the amount merely repays expenses, no charge should be brought.
Source is 廷尉信謹與丞相議曰; 信 is the personal name and 謹 modifies 與, so Xin Jin wrongly folds the adverb into the name.

Chamberlain for Law Xin Jin and the chancellor proposed: 'Officials and all ranked personnel who accept from their subordinates what they supervise, govern, execute, or command—if it is food and drink calculated to compensate for expenses, do not prosecute.

Chamberlain for Law Xin and the chancellor proposed: 'Officials and all ranked personnel who accept from their subordinates what they supervise, govern, execute, or command—if it is food and drink calculated to compensate for expenses, do not prosecute.
Source is 廷尉信謹與丞相議曰; Jin is not a name element, and dropping it corrects the invented personal name.

In the twelfth month of winter in the third year, he issued an edict: 'Xi Ping Marquis Jia's son Hui Shuo was unfilial and plotted rebellion, desiring to kill his father Jia—this constitutes great rebellion and moral depravity.

In the twelfth month of winter in the third year, he issued an edict: 'Xiangping Marquis Jia's son Hui Shuo was unfilial and plotted rebellion, desiring to kill his father Jia—this constitutes great rebellion and moral depravity.
襄平侯 is the place-name title Xiangping Marquis; splitting it as Xi Ping obscures the toponym.

In the third year, winter, twelfth month, he issued an edict saying: 'Xi Ping Marquis Jia's son Hui Shuo was unfilial, plotted rebellion, desiring to kill Jia—greatly rebellious and without moral principle.

襄平侯 should be romanized Xiangping Marquis, not the split form Xi Ping.
Therefore, pardon Jia and restore him as Xi Ping Marquis, and restore the original ranks to his wives and children who would have been implicated.
